texts: ALCAPA is the most common cause of myocardial infarction in childhood: B.

The left coronary artery, most often arising from the posterior-facing sinus of the pulmonary artery, receives low-pressure, desaturated blood; as pulmonary pressure falls in the first weeks, perfusion fails and infarction follows.
Infants are usually well at birth and present at about 6 to 8 weeks with irritability, feeding problems and heart failure, often with mitral regurgitation.
Flow then reverses: blood from the right coronary runs through collaterals into the left system and out into the pulmonary artery, a coronary steal.
In the picture, Al Capone's bolt leads to the stag falling over a child's hotel.
Memory hook: Capone's bolt is the commonest way a child's stag falls.
